Ryan Lincicum.b:
Ryan Lincicum, most recently an assistant swimming and diving coach at Towson University, has been named to the Bucknell swimming and diving coaching staff in May of 2026. Lincicum, a three-year captain at Old Dominion, helped Towson earn the Coastal Athletic Association Coaching Staff of the Year honors in his first season as a Division I coach.
Lincicum earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Psychology with minors in Exercise Science and Sports Management from Old Dominion in May of 2025. At Old Dominion, Lincicum was a four-time scorer at the Coastal Collegiate Sports Association Conference Championships and helped the Monarchs to a fourth-place team finish at the Atlantic Sun Championships in 2023-24.
A native of Burke, Va., and a graduate of Lake Braddock High School, Lincicum was a state qualifier in two events and was the Regional champion in the 200 freestyle.
Lincicum began his collegiate coaching career at Towson shortly after graduating from Old Dominion. In 2025-26, he helped lead Towson's men's and women's teams to second- and third-place finishes, respectively, at the Coastal Athletic Association Championships. The Tigers broke six school records and accomplished 22 podium finishes at the CAA Championships. Lincicum coached four U.S. Open Qualifiers and one men's NCAA championship qualifier.
While at Towson, Lincicum also served as an assistant coach for Loyola Blakefield Aquatics where he coached a practice group of athletes aged 11-14. He introduced race strategy and assisted the head coach with practice plans and training cycles.
Prior to his role Loyola Blakefield, Lincicum was also the head coach of the Highlands Swim Team in Virginia, where he coached roughly 250 athletes aged 5-18 and coordinated schedules and participation for more than 100 families. In 2025, he led the team to its best record since 2019 and helped over 20 swimmers qualify for the NVSL All-Star Meet.
While a student-athlete at Old Dominion, Lincicum was the head coach of the Burke Station Destroyers where he coached over 100 swimmers. He coordinated practice plans and schedules, and hired and managed a coaching staff of three assistants. His team held a 15-5 record and won three championships during his tenure.

Josh Huger.b:
Josh Huger, who most recently served as the associate head coach and recruiting coordinator at Cal Berkeley, was tabbed as the head coach of the Bucknell men’s and women’s swimming and diving programs on July 25, 2026.
Huger joined the Bison staff with a wealth of experience in the Division I realm, having previously served as an associate head coach at Tennessee and as an assistant coach at Virginia Tech, William & Mary, and Indiana (Pa.).
“I am thrilled to welcome Josh to the Bison Athletics family,” said vice president for athletics and recreation Tim Pavlechko. “Josh has recruited and trained championship-caliber swimmers to institutions that place a high value on the scholar-athlete experience. We are excited to have him bring that expertise and passion to the Bucknell swimming and diving program, which has a long and storied tradition of success.”
“I am incredibly honored and grateful for the opportunity to lead the Bucknell swimming and diving program,” said Huger. “I would like to thank vice president for athletics and recreation Tim Pavlechko and senior associate AD Carly Moss for their trust in me. Bucknell’s commitment to excellence, both in the classroom and in competition, makes this an incredibly special place. My family and I are thrilled to become part of the Bucknell community, and we can’t wait to get started. I’m excited to build on the strong foundation already and place and help Bucknell Swimming and Diving continue to reach new heights.”
In three seasons at Cal Berkely, Huger helped lead the Golden Bears to two men’s Atlantic Coast Conference titles and one women’s PAC-12 title. The men’s team was the national runner-up at the 2024 and 2025 NCAA Men’s Championships, and the women’s team finished fourth at the 2026 NCAA Championships. Overall, Huger led Golden Bear swimmers to four NCAA records, seven American records, two world records, two U.S. Open Records, 23 school records and eight individual NCAA titles. Since he began in July of 2023, Cal Berkely had 108 All-America performances.
Huger also served as Cal’s recruiting coordinator, where he brought in the No. 1 ranked women’s class of 2025 (SwimSwam), four No. 1 ranked recruits and 10 top-10 ranked recruits.
Huger coached in a similar role at Tennessee for four years, where the Volunteers won two women’s Southeastern Conference titles in 2020 and 2022, including an undefeated season for the women’s side in 2019-20. As the recruiting coordinator, he recruited four top-10 ranked classes and 15 top-10 recruits.
In his time at Tennessee, the Volunteers broke 84 school records, won 47 medals at the SEC Championships, and posted five top-10 finishes at NCAA tournaments. Huger focused as a sprint coach and trained the NCAA 50-yard freestyle champion, Jordan Crooks. Five student athletes broke American records, seven athletes won World Championship titles and two athletes won Olympic Medals at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. He trained the 2020, 2022 and 2023 SEC Swimmers of the Meet, and he coached three SEC Commissioner’s Trophy recipients.
Huger earned a bachelor of science degree in business administration in 2011 at Indiana University of Pennsylvania (IUP), where he competed on the men’s swimming and diving team. He then earned his master’s in sport studies in 2012 while serving as an assistant coach.
At IUP, Huger led student-athletes to an NCAA record, an NCAA title, nine All-American performances, 11 Pennsylvania State Athletic Conference titles, and four Division II NCAA qualifiers. The team set 31 school records and won its first relay title in 13 years during his time.
Huger was named an assistant coach at William & Mary in August of 2013, where he served as a sprint coach and travel coordinator. He led the men’s team to its first team title in 2015 and trained 11 CAA individual title-winners. After two years at William & Mary, Huger became an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Virginia Tech for four years. Under his leadership, the team won eight ACC individual titles, broke 44 school records, broke four ACC records and posted 16 All-America performances. Huger recruited two top-10 ranked classes, five top-10 recruits and 26 top-50 ranked recruits. He also trained 13 U.S. Open finalists, five World University Games Qualifiers and a U.S. National Team member.

Errol Carter.b:
Former University of Connecticut standout diver Errol Carter is approaching three decades of service as Bucknell's diving coach. The 2009, 2012 and 2013 Patriot League Diving Coach of the Year, Carter graduated from UConn in 1996 with a bachelor of science degree in therapeutic recreational services. He concluded an internship at the Institute of Living in Hartford in 1998, which completed his undergraduate requirements.
While at UConn, Carter was a four-year letterwinner as a diver. He advanced to the Big East finals off the three-meter board in both his sophomore (1993-94) and junior (1994-95) seasons. He was also a conference finalist off the one-meter board in 1993-94. Carter helped his team win its first New England championship in 1994-95 by placing fifth on both boards.
Carter, in 2003, helped Bison diver Adam Freeman to a Patriot League title and several school-record performances. In 2005, he coached Freeman and Erika Mannix to the NCAA Zone "A" Diving Championships. In recent years Carter helped Rebecca Bersani to four straight all-league nods, Allison FitzPatrick earn her first all-league citation as a senior in 2010 and he helped David Magaro earn all-league honors as a freshman and an NCAA Zone Diving berth as a sophomore. Carter then guided Tara Boyle and Katie Hetherington to three Patriot League titles over a two-year span. In 2025, Raggie Frias and Connor Thurston swept the Diver of the Meet honors at the ECAC Championships at Navy.
In Lewisburg, Carter volunteers his time with the community diving team, and he also helped run a diving camp at West Chester University.

Collin Hummel.b:
Collin Hummel, a 2017 graduate of Lewisburg Area High School who went on to become a two-time Division II All-American during a stellar career at Bloomsburg, joined the Bucknell coachnig staff in the fall of 2024. After graduating magna cum laude in 2022 from Bloomsburg with a degree in business administration and marketing, Hummel began his collegiate coaching career first at Millersville as a graduate assistant in 2022-23 and then as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Frostburg State in 2023-24. In his one year working with the men’s and women’s teams at Frostburg, the program recorded 24 school records and 266 lifetime bests.
Well known in the local swimming community, Hummel has also worked as an assistant coach with the Greater Susquehanna Valley YMCA and the Bison Aquatics Club. Hummel has also worked at the Navy Elite Sprint Camp, and this past June, he was an assistant coach and counselor at the University of Virginia’s Cavalier Swim Camp, where he worked directly under Virginia head coach and 2024 U.S. Olympic head coach Todd DeSorbo.
“We are excited to welcome Collin back to the Lewisburg area having grown up in the shadows of Bucknell,” said head coach Dan Schinnerer at the time of his hiring. “For a young coach, he has had great experiences and sought out good opportunities to grow as a coach. We look forward to him bringing his energy and enthusiasm to the team.”
